extra.message: Session Persistence After Account Deactivation — A deactivated user (is_active=False) can access the application with an existing session, leading to unauthorized access to sensitive data and actions. [verified: The middleware only logs out users with `is_disabled=True`, and does not check Django's built-in `User.is_active` flag. An admin deactivating a user by setting `is_active=False` (without also setting `is_disabled`) leaves the existing session valid, enabling continued access.]

Sensitive information in logs — An attacker who gains access to log files can retrieve bearer tokens and other sensitive data, potentially leading to authentication bypass. [verified: case_wire_tally_217 logs the Authorization header (line 77) without redaction, exposing bearer tokens to log files; no sanitization or access control on logs is shown, and the route is reachable via ops endpoints.]

Missing authorization on internal endpoint case_matter_file_048 — An attacker can call the endpoint without the required token, potentially gaining information about internal operations or exploiting future logic that relies on this endpoint. [verified: case_matter_file_048 does not call _wrk_gate, unlike all other ops endpoints; any unauthenticated user can access it and retrieve the user-controlled fold_ref plus a hardcoded memo, violating internal endpoint protection.]
